## Correct calls and misses

The signature failure of period 3 is **continuation shorts AFTER the
March 12-13 capitulation candle**. BTC's daily true range on the climax
day was over 4× its trailing 20-day ATR — a textbook climax event. But
the system kept generating shorts for two more weeks because daily MAs
lag:

| Coin | Date       | Direction | Entry  | SL     | TP     | Outcome   |
| ---- | ---------- | --------- | ------ | ------ | ------ | --------- |
| BTC  | 2020-03-09 | short     | 8081   | 8789   | 6667   | correct   |
| BTC  | 2020-03-16 | short     | 5254   | 5940   | 3884   | **WRONG** |
| BTC  | 2020-03-23 | short     | 5904   | 6408   | 4896   | **WRONG** |
| ETH  | 2020-03-02 | short     | 218.92 | 227.89 | 200.98 | **WRONG** |
| ETH  | 2020-03-09 | short     | 203.14 | 234.19 | 141.04 | correct   |
| ETH  | 2020-03-16 | short     | 121.60 | 133.50 | 97.80  | **WRONG** |
| ETH  | 2020-03-23 | short     | 124.12 | 137.13 | 98.10  | **WRONG** |

The pre-climax short on 03-09 caught the move. Every short *after* the
climax was stopped out as price reverted into the pre-crash range.
**Five of the eleven losing trades for the period are post-climax
shorts within two weeks of the bottom**, and three more are
April-June continuation longs whose SL got hit during the choppy
recovery (BTC 05-18, 06-08; ETH 04-20, 04-27, 05-18, 06-08).

This is not a re-entry-discipline failure (iter 3 already covers
that). This is a regime-detection failure: the system has no concept
of "the regime just changed in a single candle, stand down".

## What changed and why

**One concrete theory improvement:** added
`market_phase_discipline.post_climax_cooldown` to `docs/technical.yaml`.

The new section formalizes the previously qualitative "never enter
during momentum" guidance into a measurable, dated suspension:

> After a CLIMAX EVENT — single daily candle whose true range exceeds
> 3× trailing 20-day ATR, OR weekly true range exceeding 2× the trailing
> 20-week ATR — all entries in the direction of the climax (continuation)
> AND all counter-climax entries are SUSPENDED until one of three reset
> conditions holds: a daily structure reset back inside the pre-climax
> range, ten quiet trading days, or a fresh weekly close against the
> climax direction.

The block includes:

- The climax-event definition with explicit ATR multipliers.
- The three reset conditions (a)(b)(c).
- A rationale linked directly to the BTC and ETH 03-16 / 03-23 entries
  in this backtest, with the dollar amounts.
- A how-to-apply block describing the rolling ATR computation and the
  "freeze flag" semantics.
- A relationship_to_existing_rules block clarifying that this is
  strictly tighter than the qualitative momentum rule, dominates
  re_entry_discipline (iter 3) when both apply, and operationalizes
  volatility_deep_dive's previously orientation-only ATR hint.
- A note_for_engines block specifying that the freeze flag must
  dominate both the weekly bias call and the 4H setup check — even if
  every other condition passes, the freeze forces "no entry".

### Why this is the right theory improvement for 2020-Q1

The dominant trade-level failure (×11 stopped trades) is the
post-capitulation short cluster plus the post-recovery long cluster.
Both are downstream of the same root cause: the system has no concept
of "the regime just inverted on a single candle". Adding regime
detection in the form of an ATR-based climax flag is the most direct
fix.

This rule does NOT solve the May/June chop losses (BTC 05-18, 06-08
longs; ETH 04-20, 04-27, 05-18, 06-08 longs). Those are slow-grind
failures that look more like the 2019-recovery pyramiding pattern —
already covered by iter 3's `re_entry_discipline`. The post-climax
rule is specifically targeted at the March 16 / March 23 cluster, the
only ones that are NOT explained by the prior iterations.

## 4H/1H execution notes

- The 03-09 BTC short worked exactly as designed: weekly bias short,
  daily confirmation, 4H setup, 1H trigger, TP at $6667 hit. The model
  IS capable of catching a black-swan move when it enters BEFORE the
  climax.
- The 03-16 and 03-23 entries are textbook examples of "MA-based bias
  lagging the regime change" — a categorical limitation of any system
  that derives bias from a moving average. The post-climax cooldown
  bridges that lag by suspending entries during the recovery rather
  than waiting for the MA to catch up.
- ETH's 03-02 short (entry $218.92, before the climax) was already a
  loser — pre-climax overreach in the slow grind into the crash. Not
  addressed by today's rule and worth flagging for a future iteration
  on "early-stage shorts before the volatility expansion".

## Open questions for later iterations

1. **Slow-grind chop in recovery**: BTC May-June longs and ETH
   April-June longs would benefit from a regime-classifier
   improvement that does NOT trigger on a single candle.
2. **The 03-02 ETH pre-climax short**: a separate pattern — entries
   into accumulating volatility before the expansion is visible. Hard
   to address without forward information.
3. **SL placement in post-climax expansion**: BTC's 03-16 SL was
   $5940 — only 13% above an entry on a day when daily ATR was
   probably 25-40%. Even with the cooldown rule, SL placement
   matters; carry over.
